pageRules.note: Confirmed from the live glofox.com grid: max-width 1280px, 16px side padding, 1248px usable content width. Every section — including NavBar and Footer — aligns its inner content to this same width; a section may paint a full-bleed background, but its content never aligns to the section's own edge. Applied as --container-max-width/--container-padding tokens, wired into a `.inner` wrapper in every full-bleed page-section component: NavBar, Footer, Hero, UtilityBar. The audit callout on this page found NavBar/Footer/dark-NavBar each using a different, non-matching width in the Figma file itself (1200px canvas with 64px/80px/24px padding) — none of those mismatched values were carried into code; this repo's NavBar/Footer now consistently use the confirmed 1280/16 rule. Excluded Carousel (a self-bounded, padded widget) — it doesn't own a full-bleed background the way the others do. (PromoBanner, ResourcesHero, ResourceCardGrid, ResourceCarouselSection — the other components this rule originally called out — were removed from Figma and deleted from the repo on 2026-08-26; see removedComponents.)

Two Hero image layouts are documented: NO1 (50/50 split, image caps at max-width 590px / min-width 350px, drops below the title at tablet, never cropped — only scaled) and NO2 (image sits full-width below the title, matching the page container width at every breakpoint). NOT applied to code: src/components/Hero has no image slot at all currently, so there's nothing yet to size-constrain. Flagging this rather than inventing an image feature that wasn't asked for — if/when Hero gets an image prop, implement it under one of these two layouts rather than a new one.
